reasoning:
An 8-digit number with nondecreasing digits has all digits in 1..9 (leading digit nonzero forces every digit >=1). So we count multisets of 8 digits from {1..9} with sum 40. Subtracting 1 from each digit: multisets of 8 values in {0..8} summing to 32, i.e. partitions of 32 into at most 8 parts each <=8 (an 8x8 box). Grouped by k = number of nonzero parts (i.e. number of digits >=2), with the k parts in [1,8] summing to 32 (k>=4 since 8*4=32):

k=4: 8+8+8+8 only -> 1.
k=5: set part=8-x, x>=0, sum x = 8, x<=7, at most 5 parts: partitions of 8 into <=5 parts (18) minus '8' -> 17.
k=6: x sum 16, <=6 parts each <=7 = P(16;6,7). By largest part: 7->21, 6->23, 5->19, 4->11, 3->2; total 76.
k=7: P(24;7,7). By largest part: 7->P(17;6,7)=81 (sub-cases 26+25+20+9+1), 6->P(18;6,6)=58 (29+20+8+1), 5->P(19;6,5)=30 (24+6), 4->P(20;6,4)=5; total 174.
k=8: P(24;8,7) = P(24;7,7) + P(16;8,6) = 174 + 93 (P(16;8,6) by largest part: 6->31, 5->30, 4->22, 3->9, 2->1) = 267.

Total = 1 + 17 + 76 + 174 + 267 = 535.

Sanity check: this is the central coefficient (q^32) of the Gaussian binomial [16 choose 8]_q, whose 12870 total coefficients have variance 8*8*17/12 ~ 90.7 (sigma ~ 9.5), giving a predicted peak ~ 12870/(sqrt(2*pi)*9.5) ~ 539, consistent with 535.
